description:
In August 1998 Larry Page and Sergey Brin published the first Doodle to say they were away at Burning Man. Google's Doodles page dates it to 30 August 1998.

Asked by Page and Brin to design a Bastille Day logo in 2000, his first Doodle.

The first animated Doodle ran on 31 October 2000, for Halloween. The first interactive one came ten years later.

On 21 May 2010 a playable Pac-Man logo marked the game's 30th anniversary. Google calls it the first interactive Doodle game experience.

Google says it has made more than this over the decades.

Sources:
- https://doodles.google/about/ (read): established that the first Doodle was published in 1998, dated 30 August 1998, so the founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin could tell people they were out of office for Burning Man, that the team has created more than 5,000 Doodles, and that the Pac-Man Doodle of 21 May 2010 was the first interactive Doodle game experience.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Doodle (read): independently established the Burning Man origin, that Page and Brin later asked Dennis Hwang to design a Bastille Day logo in 2000, that the first animated Doodle ran on 31 October 2000, and that the first interactive Doodle was the playable Pac-Man logo of 21 May 2010.
